search_entities.description: Search any MusicBrainz index with a query you write yourself. The dedicated searches build the query from labelled fields; this one takes MusicBrainz's own search syntax and reaches the indexes they do not cover - areas, events, places, instruments, series, URLs, annotations, tags and CD stubs. The query is sent exactly as written, so its syntax is yours to get right; MusicBrainz documents the fields each index accepts.

results.name: Abbey Road Studios

submit_barcode.description: Attach the EAN or UPC printed on a release's packaging. Only GTIN codes are accepted, and the check digit is verified before sending so a typo is caught here rather than refused there. Unlike a tag or a rating this changes the database for everyone, so it opens an edit: it applies once it goes unopposed or its voting period expires.
submit_barcode.display_name: Add a barcode to a release
submit_barcode.name: submit_barcode

parameters.description: The release's MusicBrainz ID, or the address of its page. A release is one issue of an album; the ID of the album itself is a release group ID and will not be found here.
parameters.name: release_id

parameters.description: The 8, 12, 13 or 14 digit GTIN. Spaces and hyphens are ignored. Codes with a 2 or 5 digit add-on are not accepted by MusicBrainz.
parameters.name: barcode

submit_isrcs.description: Attach one or more ISRCs to a recording. Each code is checked against the ISRC format first, and the hyphens a printed ISRC carries are dropped. Like a barcode this opens an edit rather than applying at once.
submit_isrcs.name: submit_isrcs

parameters.description: The recording's MusicBrainz ID, or the address of its page. A recording is one performance, as it appears as a track.
parameters.name: recording_id

parameters.description: The codes to attach: one per line, comma-separated, or a list from an earlier step. Hyphens are optional.
parameters.name: isrcs

submit_rating.description: Rate a MusicBrainz entity out of five stars as the connected account. Ratings take effect at once and feed the community average. Choosing no rating removes yours rather than recording a bad one. Areas, places, releases and series cannot be rated: rate the release group rather than one of its issues.
submit_rating.name: submit_rating

parameters.description: Which kind of entity the ID names.
parameters.name: entity_type

options.label: Artist - a person, group or orchestra

parameters.description: The entity's MusicBrainz ID, or the musicbrainz.org address of its page. It must be an ID of the kind chosen above: MusicBrainz IDs are not shared between kinds of entity.
parameters.name: mbid

parameters.description: How many stars to give it. MusicBrainz stores this out of 100 behind the scenes; whole stars are all it ever collects.
parameters.name: rating

submit_tags.description: Add tags to a MusicBrainz entity, hide ones you disagree with, or take back a vote you cast before. Tags are public and attributed to your account, and take effect at once. Genres are submitted the same way: a tag drawn from MusicBrainz's genre list counts as a genre.
submit_tags.name: submit_tags

parameters.description: Which kind of entity the ID names.
parameters.name: entity_type

options.label: Area - a country, city or region
Artist - a person, group or orchestra

Label - a record label or imprint
Place - a venue, studio or stadium

Release - one issue of an album, with its own barcode
Release group - an album, across all its issues
Series - a run of related releases or events
Work - the composition itself, behind its recordings
URL - a web address linked to something

parameters.description: The entity's MusicBrainz ID, or the musicbrainz.org address of its page. It must be an ID of the kind chosen above: MusicBrainz IDs are not shared between kinds of entity.

description: Look up music metadata in MusicBrainz, the open music encyclopedia: search for artists, albums, recordings, works and labels; read an artist's full discography or a label's catalogue; follow the relationships that record who played on what and where a release streams; identify a CD from its disc ID or a recording from its ISRC; fetch cover art; read your own collections; and submit tags, ratings, ISRCs and barcodes.
